parsed.md:
## Start here

Altered Audio Editor is a free, open-source multitrack audio editor for podcasters and voiceover. It works like the editors you may know from Adobe Audition, with extras made for spoken word.

![The Multitrack Editor: 1 the ruler, 2 a track header, 3 a clip and 4 the playhead](editor-overview)

There are two editors.

- The **Multitrack Editor** is where you build an episode: tracks, clips, effects, mixing and export.
- The **Waveform Editor** edits one audio file at a time, down to the sample. Switch with View > Switch Between Editors, or pick one from the View menu.

Your first episode in five steps:

1. Choose File > New Session, pick a name and a sample rate (48000 Hz is a good default), and press OK.
2. Bring in audio with File > Import Files, or drag files from your file manager into the window. Use Multitrack > Insert Files as Tracks to put each file on its own track.
3. Press the space bar to play and stop. Click in the ruler to move the playhead.
4. Fix what you hear: split clips at the playhead (Clip > Split at Playhead), trim edges, and add effects in the Voice Chain.
5. When it sounds right, choose File > Export > Session Mixdown.

Save often with File > Save. While there are unsaved changes the program also keeps a recovery copy, and offers to recover it if it did not close normally.

Opening files: one audio file opens in the Waveform Editor as itself, and two or more build a Multitrack session.

- A video file opens as a picture to cut against (see Video). With two or more sessions open, a tab for each runs along the top of the Multitrack.
- File > Open Recent keeps sessions and audio files. Sessions saved by other editors open too: File > Import Session (.sesx) reads Audition's session files, and File > Import Session (.rpp) reads projects from another editor, bringing tracks, clips, fades, markers and regions (plug-ins, sends and automation are left out, and the notice says what was left behind).

New sessions can start from a template. File > New Session offers Two-Host Show, Solo Voiceover and Audiobook, and File > Save as Session Template makes your own. Templates are ordinary: rename, change or delete them.

If you open a session made by an older version, nothing changes until you save.

- Saving upgrades it and keeps the original in the Backups folder, named with the old version, and a notice says so.
- Older versions of Altered Audio cannot open a session once it is upgraded. If the backup cannot be made, the save is stopped and your file is left as it was.

## Privacy

There is no account, no sign-in, no tracking and no telemetry.

- Your audio and sessions stay on your computer. The program goes online only when you choose Help > Check for Updates or open a link from the Help menu.
- There is also an update notice that is off until you turn it on in Settings > Privacy. Pick every start or once a week. When a newer version exists, a small notice appears in the bottom right corner with a button to see what is new. You can also tick "Install it for me when the program starts": the update is then checked against the project's signing key and installed at start-up (installed copies only), after asking about any unsaved work. Otherwise nothing installs until you click Install and Restart, and with the notice off the program never goes online by itself.

## Recording

Add a track with Multitrack > Add > Mono Track or Stereo Track, then arm it with the **R** button in its header.

- Pick the input in the track header. Press Record (Multitrack > Record) and press Stop when you are done.
- The take lands on the armed track as a new clip at the playhead.

Recording Options (Multitrack > Recording Options) holds pre-roll, punch-in and the recording offset.

- With a time selection, Record starts a pre-roll before it, stops by itself at the end and replaces what was there on the recorded tracks (punch-in).
- The offset trims a few milliseconds from the start of each take so takes line up with what they were played against.

To record a call, each output device is also offered as an input named "System audio" followed by the device. It records what the computer plays, while microphones record on their own tracks.

**Marking while you record.** Three quick marks drop a numbered marker at the playhead: Add Retake Marker (F6), Add Cut This Marker (Shift+F6) and Add Great Bit Marker (Ctrl+F6). They work in the Multitrack and in the Waveform Editor, and every key can be changed in Keyboard Shortcuts. Window > Review lists your Cut this, Retake and Great bit marks in time order, with Previous and Next to step through them and a filter to show one kind.

**Scrubbing.** Settings > Playback and Recording has Play audio while scrubbing. With it on, dragging the playhead along the ruler plays what is under it. It is approximate: playback restarts at the pointer every moment. It is off by default.

**Playback speed.** Settings > Playback and Recording has Playback speed (experimental). With it on, Transport > Playback Speed plays the mix from 0.5x to 2x with the pitch kept, which is handy for reviewing speech. It is for listening only: recording, exports and saved files are not affected. At 0.5x and 2x the sound is smeared, the metronome is silent whenever the speed is not Normal, and it does not apply to 3D Space sessions heard on speakers. Recording puts it back to Normal, and so does starting the program again.

## Tracks, clips and editing

A **track** holds clips. A **clip** is a piece of an audio file placed on the timeline. Cutting a clip never changes the file on disk.

- Split at the playhead with Clip > Split at Playhead, or all clips at once with Split All Clips at Playhead.
- Drag a clip to move it. Lock Position keeps a clip where it is.
- Drag the small square handles in a clip's title bar to set its fade in and fade out. New fades start as an S curve, which sounds smooth on speech.
- Ripple editing (Edit > Ripple Delete) closes the gap when you delete, so the rest of the episode slides left.
- Snap (Edit > Snap) pulls edges to clips, the playhead, markers or ruler ticks.
- Undo and Redo cover every edit. A fader drag or a recorded automation take is one step.

**Closing gaps.** Click an empty space between two clips and it lights up. Press Delete (or use Edit > Ripple Delete > Gap Between Clips) and the clips after it slide left to close it. Undo puts everything back.

![Click the gap between clips and press Delete: everything after it slides left](ripple-gap)

**Ripple Delete a time selection.** Drag across a stretch of time, then choose one of the Ripple Delete commands. Time Selection in Selected Clips (Alt+Backspace) cuts that stretch out of only the clips you selected and slides the later clips on their tracks left. Time Selection in Selected Track and in All Tracks cut whole tracks.

**Sync Lock** keeps tracks in step. The chain-link button in a track's header turns it on or off. When you ripple on a track with Sync Lock on, every other track with Sync Lock on closes the same stretch, so music and voices do not drift apart. A track with it off is left alone. New sessions start with Sync Lock on for the first tracks; tracks you add later start with it off.

![With Sync Lock on, a ripple delete on Voice closes the same time on Music; with it off, Music is left behind](sync-lock)

If a Sync Lock track has audio in the space you are closing, the program stops and says so, because closing it would cut or misalign that track. Turn Sync Lock off for that track to close the gap on one track only.

Press **I** to set the start of the time selection at the playhead and **O** to set the end. Shift+I and Shift+O clear them. With no end set the selection runs to the end of the content. They work in both editors.

Markers (Edit > Add Marker) can mark cues, chapters, ad slots and social clips. Chapters and ad slots can be exported from File > Export > Markers and Chapters.

In the Markers panel, click a marker to pick it and jump to it.

- Right-click a marker flag on the ruler, or a row in the panel, for Go to Marker, Rename, Convert to Range or Point, Change Marker Type and Delete.
- The panel has End and Description columns, a search box and resizable columns. Ctrl+click adds or removes one, and Shift+click picks a run.
- Edit > Markers > Rename Selected Marker, Delete Selected Markers and Delete All Markers work on the pick, and Undo brings them back.

**Track Visibility.** Multitrack > Track Visibility hides tracks from the Editor and Mixer lists without stopping them from playing. Save Visibility Preset remembers which tracks are hidden under a name, and Load Visibility Preset brings it back. Presets match tracks by name, so a preset made for one episode works in the next one. The newest eight are kept.

**Groups.** Group Clips (Clip > Group) ties clips together so clicking one picks them all and they move as one. Suspend Groups (Ctrl+Shift+G) turns that off for a while so you can pick a single clip without breaking the group. Remove Focus Clip from Group takes just the clip you clicked last out of its group, and Ungroup Selected Clips takes out every clip you have picked.

**Meter Input Signal** (Multitrack > Meter Input Signal, Alt+I) shows the input level on every track, not only the armed ones, so you can check a mic before you arm it.

**Host profiles and Guest Track.** Multitrack > Host Profile gives a voice track a starting Voice Chain set for how that person sounds: Close Mic, Standard Mic or Remote Guest.

- It replaces the track's chain in one undo step, and Clear Profile takes it away. Remote Guest uses stronger noise and room cleanup, a gentler gate and a low-pass that keeps call fizz out above 7 kHz, and marks the track as a guest track.
- Multitrack > Add > Guest Track adds a mono track named Guest with that profile already on, ready for a guest's recording.

## Takes and comping

![Three takes of one line, then a time selection comped from Take 2](takes-comping)

When you record a line more than once, put the takes on one track over the same stretch, select those clips and choose Clip > Make Takes from Selected Clips. They become a set of takes: only one plays, and the others stay on the track, drawn dim. The **Takes** panel (Window > Takes) lists each set.

To comp, make a time selection over the part you like and press **Use over selection** beside that take.

- The editor cuts the takes at the edges of the selection and switches which one plays, as one undo step.
- With no selection, **Use** plays that take over the whole stretch. A take is cut back to the audio it actually has, so nothing goes silent by accident.
- Each piece is an ordinary clip, so you can still move, trim, fade or split it.

**Flatten** removes the takes that are not playing and turns the rest into ordinary clips.

- **Delete** removes one take. Settings > Multitrack turns the take commands off if you never use them; sessions that already have takes still play the chosen ones.
- Mixdowns and .sesx exports leave out takes that are not playing. A session that has takes plays every take at once in older versions of the program.

## Multi-mic shows

![Two mics hear both people; Reduce Bleed and Auto Mic Mix tidy it up](multi-mic)

These tools are for a conversation recorded with one mic per person, or a call recorded twice (a double-ender). Each works on the whole session and is one undo step.

- **Reduce Bleed** (Multitrack > Reduce Bleed) cleans one mic's track against another's, taking out the other voice that leaked in while keeping the voice on this mic, even when both talk at once. Each clip is cleaned into a copy in a Bleed Reduced folder beside your session. Your originals are not changed. Run it before Auto Mic Mix, and use Sync Tracks first if the tracks are not in step.
- **Auto Mic Mix and Talk Time** (Multitrack > Auto Mic Mix and Talk Time) finds who is talking and writes a volume lane on each mic that turns it down while someone else speaks. When

that keeps call fizz out above 7 khz, and marks the track as a guest track. multitrack > add > guest track adds a mono track named guest with that profile already on, ready for a guest's recording.

out.title: Multi-mic shows

blocks.alt: Two mics hear both people; Reduce Bleed and Auto Mic Mix tidy it up
blocks.name: multi-mic

spans.text: These tools are for a conversation recorded with one mic per person, or a call recorded twice (a double-ender). Each works on the whole session and is one undo step.

items.text: Reduce Bleed

(Multitrack > Reduce Bleed) cleans one mic's track against another's, taking out the other voice that leaked in while keeping the voice on this mic, even when both talk at once. Each clip is cleaned into a copy in a Bleed Reduced folder beside your session. Your originals are not changed. Run it before Auto Mic Mix, and use Sync Tracks first if the tracks are not in step.
Auto Mic Mix and Talk Time
